correctness.rationale: For all 771 connected labeled graphs of order 2–5, open-edge outcome enumeration yields exact integer degree-at-most-six outbreak polynomials. The pairwise connectivity identity independently checks every component-square score. Degree-six rational projective transforms produce nonnegative integer coefficients for every optimal-vs-other placement comparison on both p-intervals; 6,932 strict comparison certificates replay successfully. Two exceptional canonical graph types have exact factors 2p²(1−4p) and 2p²(1−p)(1−4p), and the endpoint tie sets are separately checked. Finite enumeration proves precisely the bounded claim and does not claim larger orders.

evidence: Holme (2017) analyzes continuous-time Markov SIR vaccination on small graphs and is especially relevant by graph order, but shared exponential recovery makes edge transmissions from the same infective dependent. Two independent bond successes have probability β²/(1+β)² after p=β/(1+β); in the Markov SIR model the probability of infecting both susceptible neighbors is 2β²/((1+β)(1+2β)), generally different.
Masuda (2009) considers immunization heuristics in networks with community structure and associated fragmentation/spectral measures, not the enumerated uniform-seed final outbreak size.
Morone–Makse (2015) targets optimal percolation or giant-component fragmentation in larger networks, not the finite exact expected outbreak-size ranking.
Bucur–Holme (2020) abstract concerns epidemic source importance and centrality prediction over graphs through order ten, rather than the one-vertex deletion minimization considered here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Holme provides substantial overlapping finite-graph motivation but neither its Markov SIR law nor its resulting objective table implies the exact independent Bernoulli-bond classification by a universal parameter change. There remains an explicit historical risk that earlier reliability literature solved the same independent-bond objective.

originality.rationale: The original assertion is the sharp graph-order onset, the exactly two graph classes and their complete all-p optimum sets in independent bond SIR. Newman’s bond mapping, general percolation theory and the outbreak-score identity are not original. Holme’s most closely related exact small-graph study assumes continuous-time Markov SIR and correlated transmission through a shared random recovery period; it cannot imply the independent-bond classification by rescaling transmission rate. Searches and inspected primary material did not identify an equivalent prior result; historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: An older finite-graph network reliability or vaccination table could already encode this exact independent-edge ranking.
Holme 2017 treats related vaccination problems on the same small graph orders; its results differ in epidemic law, but independent historical interpretation remains necessary.
The literature corpus and published-record match search are incomplete; lack of match does not prove originality.
Bucur–Holme 2020 studies exact small-graph epidemic importance but only the abstract was accessible in this pass; no whole-document noncoverage claim is made.

value.rationale: Optimizing expected final infections under one fully protective node is a natural vaccination-placement benchmark. The result is a sharp complete smallest-order boundary, not a hand-picked graph numerical curiosity: all connected graphs through four vertices have transmissibility-independent optima, exactly two five-vertex types change and both have the same exact switch 1/4. Their contenders have equal degrees, exposing a natural limitation of degree centrality without claiming realistic clinical policy impact.
